html:
Samudragupta was the second emperor of the Gupta Empire in north India. He ruled from about 335 to 375 and made the Guptas the leading power in the subcontinent. His birth date is unknown.

He was the son of Chandragupta I and the Licchavi princess Kumaradevi. Most of what we know comes from a long Sanskrit praise poem by his court poet Harishena, carved on an older Ashoka pillar now in the fort at Allahabad, today's Prayagraj. It lists his wins:

  • Kings of the Ganges plain, uprooted and their lands annexed.
  • Kings of the south, as far as Kanchipuram of the Pallavas, defeated and then restored as tributaries.
  • Forest peoples and frontier kingdoms that paid tribute.
  • Distant rulers, from the Kushan lands to Sri Lanka, said to have sent gifts.

His gold coins show him as a horse sacrificer, an archer, and playing the vina, a lute. He was both conqueror and patron of learning. His son Chandragupta II carried the empire to its height, the age of Kalidasa.
sum: Samudragupta was the second emperor of the Gupta Empire in north India. He ruled from about 335 to 375 and made the Guptas the leading power in the subcontinent. His birth date is unknown.
